title: BeatBoard Studio: Implement Multi-Session Project Template System
description: BeatBoard Studio is a desktop music production application. A highly requested feature is the ability to create, save, and load 'Project Templates'. These templates would allow users to pre-configure a project with specific settings like BPM, time signature, a default set of audio tracks, and pre-loaded plugins/effects, saving them significant setup time. This task requires implementing this feature incrementally over several development sessions, touching on data modeling, file I/O, state management, and UI integration.

project_spec.name: BeatBoard Studio
project_spec.description:
BeatBoard Studio is a desktop-productivity application that blurs the line between work and play by transforming everyday note-taking and task organization into an audio-visual experience. Rather than simple text lists, each note or to-do item is represented as a ‘beat block’ that can be snapped onto a time-line or grid; as users arrange, complete, or defer tasks, the blocks trigger sound effects, short music loops, or light animations—turning daily productivity into an entertaining, almost gamified jam session. The program supports multiple windows (e.g., Mixer, Scheduler, Theme Designer, Plugin Hub) and lets users pick from colorful entertainment-oriented themes reminiscent of DJ consoles, retro arcades, or sci-fi holodecks.

Underlying this playful facade is a strictly component-based architecture: every functional slice (beat-rendering, audio engine, note persistence, plugin loader, theme manager, settings controller, update agent, etc.) is encapsulated in a well-defined, swappable component. Developers and ambitious users can extend the app by writing plug-ins that add new sound packs, visualizers, or even entirely new task-management paradigms—not unlike adding new instruments to a digital audio workstation. Settings, user preferences, and themes are stored in isolated configuration components; auto-update logic is an event-driven service component that quietly checks, downloads, and hot-swaps updated bundles in the background, ensuring the groove never stops.
dependencies: GTK 4.x (GUI framework, supports multi-window, high-resolution animations)
cJSON (lightweight JSON parsing for user_preferences and settings_configuration)
libcurl (auto_updates: secure download of component bundles)
SQLite (embedded database for tasks and user data)
libadwaita (optional modern theming layer on top of GTK)
